how: A local server answered three origins, www.example.com and api.example.com (one site) and www.example.net (another), mapped to 127.0.0.1 with --host-resolver-rules, and localhost, over HTTPS with HTTP/2 or with HTTP/1.1 only, and over plain HTTP, where it answered app.localhost, 127.0.0.1 and [::1] too; it kept every request as the bytes said it, headers in order with their values, and HTTP/2 the priority of its HEADERS frame (exclusive, stream it depends on, weight as on the wire). Each scenario ran in a fresh profile: a URL opened from the command line, or a page whose script navigated, submitted a form, called fetch() or sent an XHR. A page under /auth/ answered 401, with a Basic challenge of the realm "bench" (after a Digest one where the scenario says so), until it was sent u:p; a page under /digest/ asked for Digest authentication of that realm as its offer said, checking each answer as RFC 7616 has a server check one, until it was answered with u:p, and then went on by a URL without credentials. The pages that ran them, and the requests that set cookies for them, are left out, as are the port numbers.
